title: The Natyashastra
author: bharata
attributionNote: Ascribed to the sage Bharata, to whom tradition also gives a hundred sons who recited it. The text is a compilation that grew over centuries.
description: The Natyashastra is the oldest surviving treatise on drama, dance and music in the world: the origin of the theatre and its sacred uses, the training of actors, the structure of plays and the theory of plot, the gestures of the hands and the movements of the body, the modes and the emotions with their corresponding states, costume, ornament, make-up, the stage and its architecture, and music with its scales and rhythms.
historicalContext: Everything later written on Indian performance takes the Natyashastra as its point of departure: classical dance, Sanskrit drama and Indian music theory all name its chapters. Its theory of the eight or nine rasa, the emotions a performance should evoke, became the central idea of Indian aesthetics.
availabilityNote: Complete: the Sanskrit verses of the chapters GRETIL publishes, streamed from GRETIL at read time, one chapter at a time. This is the original Sanskrit, not a translation.
